title: Research method for Atrial fibrillation predicted effector genes (Roselli et al., 2018)
bodyHtml:
These results were generated in the study:

Multi-ethnic genome-wide association study for atrial fibrillation.
Roselli C, et al.
Nat Genet. 2018 Sep;50(9):1225-1233. doi: 10.1038/s41588-018-0133-9.
PMID: 29892015

The GWAS meta-analysis performed in this study (integrated into the Knowledge Portals as AF HRC GWAS) included 65,446 individuals with atrial fibrillation (AF) and 522,744 controls.

At loci with a genome-wide significant association for AF, the following analyses were performed:

  • The nearest gene to the sentinel variant was identified.
  • GTEx Heart Expression (left ventricle and atrial appendage): genes are listed if within 500KB of the sentinel variant and gene expression for at least one heart tissue in GTEx (version 6p) is in the top 5 and median (RMPK) > 1.
  • Gene set enrichment analysis using the MAGENTA (Meta-Analysis Gene-set Enrichment of variaNT Associations) v2.4 method (Segre AV et al, 2010). Genes were prioritized if they were within 500kb of the sentinel variant and were present in at least one enriched pathway. A total of 55 enriched gene sets or pathways were identified, that largely fall into cardiac developmental, electrophysiological, and cardiomyocyte contractile or structural functional groups.
  • eQTL MAGNet Left Atrial: listed genes are eGenes for eQTLs in left atrial tissue from the Myocardial Applied Genomics Network (MAGNet) repository that overlap with atrial fibrillation GWAS signals. "Protective" indicates that higher gene expression associates with decreased AF risk, while "Risk" indicates that higher gene expression associates with increased AF risk.
  • eQTL GTEx Heart (left ventricle and atrial appendage): listed genes are eGenes for eQTLs in left ventricle and atrial appendage from GTEx (version 6p) that overlap with atrial fibrillation GWAS signals.
  • MetaXcan Heart (left ventricle and atrial appendage): genes are listed whose transcription level in heart left ventricle and atrial appendage was predicted by MetaXcan analysis (Barbeira AN et al., 2018) to be associated with AF disease risk.
